candidate.title: Recursive normative self-conformance
candidate.problemStatement: A normative system can impose exact conformance on adopters while reconstructing or bypassing those duties when changing its own rules.
candidate.scope: Pre-number KFD self-change from exact genesis through qualification, independent review, authority-separated disposition, and explicit admission or retained non-promotion; numbering, activation, merge, and release remain outside the candidate.

observationPerspective.role: change the normative system after the Self-Conformance Profile became load-bearing
consequences: must distinguish structural validity from semantic and governance authority
must preserve historical coordinates while admitting a successor cut

currentOntology: KFD-1 fact cuts and compatibility boundaries
KFD-11 claim, assessment, decision, and admission
Self-Conformance transition bundles and lifecycle gates
genesis.observation: The recursive path is useful but currently distributed across normative decisions and a repository Profile, creating repeated reconstruction pressure and a risk that Profile verification is mistaken for semantic or governance authority.
genesis.candidateObject: A procedure requiring load-bearing normative self-change to use the same fixed-root, authority-separated conformance path required of adopters.
genesis.claimBoundary: Genesis proposes a testable composition and does not claim irreducibility, universality, historical execution before the Profile existed, qualification, numbering, activation, merge, or release.
genesis.methodNotes: Reconstruction pressure generates the candidate; structural compression compares a new named procedure with the existing KFD-1/KFD-2/KFD-5/KFD-11 closure.

contactSides: governance changes made by the normative system
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: Maintainers and agents reconstruct the self-application path from multiple decisions, repository rules, review conventions, and verifier outputs.

pressureChanges.description: Successor agents must recover authority boundaries without private maintainer context.
A structural verifier can appear authoritative even though it cannot decide semantic truth, numbering, activation, merge, or release.

observedFailures: Passing structural reports can be overstated as qualification.
Retrospective reconstruction can be mislabeled as historical execution.
One actor can be described under multiple role names and mistaken for independent review.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: An explicit recursive path may keep fixed evidence, structural verification, review, disposition, and admission independently inspectable.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: Treat the path as the composed application of KFD-1, KFD-2, KFD-5, KFD-11, and the Self-Conformance Profile without a new KFD.

pressure: The Self-Conformance Profile already processes KFD lifecycle changes but cannot supply semantic or governance authority.
Historical KFD changes predate the Profile and require typed non-retroactive replay.
The proposed procedure may duplicate the existing normative closure.
grounding.evidenceBoundary: Public files in the exact genesis commit and immutable historical Git/review coordinates cited by them; no private transcript, live network state, or later review is included.
knownGaps: Independent qualification review is not yet retained.
No non-KFD adopter reproduces the candidate as an irreducible object.
Historical KFD-1 through KFD-3 bootstrap did not run the later Self-Conformance Profile.

alternatives.name: New numbered KFD procedure
alternatives.reason: Would make recursive self-application explicit but must first prove an independent responsibility beyond existing KFDs.

alternatives.name: KFD-1, KFD-2, KFD-5, and KFD-11 composition
alternatives.reason: Already supplies exact cuts, fact-bound assessment, genesis/qualification separation, and decision/admission separation.

alternatives.name: Self-Conformance Profile only
alternatives.reason: Supplies deterministic structural machinery but cannot become normative, semantic, or governance authority.

alternatives.name: No explicit self-conformance path
alternatives.reason: Leaves repeated reconstruction and authority confusion unaddressed even if no new KFD is ultimately justified.

contractModel.identity: One pre-number recursive normative self-conformance Candidate bound to an exact genesis cut.
contractModel.boundary: Normative self-change only; adopter implementations, numbering, activation, protected merge, and release remain under their own authorities.
contractModel.authority: Genesis author, structural verifier, independent reviewer, disposition authority, repository admission, and release authority remain distinct.
contractModel.lifecycle: absent -> candidate -> qualified, provisional, rejected, or no-new-kfd -> optional separately authorized promotion and admission

minimumClosure.notes: The minimum useful path is explicit; whether it requires a new Primitive remains unresolved.

deletion.notes: Analytic deletion preserves every current decision observation, favoring derivability pending independent review.

fuse.notes: The candidate fuses into the existing normative closure without contradiction, but the Profile alone cannot own normative authority.

falsifiers: A fixed-root decision changes when the Candidate is deleted while KFD-1, KFD-2, KFD-5, KFD-11, and the Profile remain available.
A non-KFD adopter requires an independent recursive identity, boundary, authority, lifecycle, or operation that the existing closure cannot express.
Fusing the Candidate into existing KFDs creates unavoidable authority ambiguity.
The fixed package cannot fail closed on root, predecessor, review, authority, package, or claim substitution without a new normative contract.
No new KFD is justified if deletion preserves every decision observation and the Candidate only names the existing composition.

dogfood.notes: The first recursive run is open. Structural and clean-room evidence plus independent review are still required.

decision.reason: The candidate is generated and analytically favors derivability, but the fixed-root replay, clean-room verification, native/WASM parity, independent review, and authority-separated terminal disposition are not yet retained.
residualRisks: Role labels may be mistaken for actual independent authority.
Retrospective replay may be overstated as historical conformance.
A useful named composition may be over-promoted into a redundant KFD.
